MANILA, Philippines – Last November 12, the Choco Mucho Flying Titans erupted in joy as they downed their “big sisters” Creamline Cool Smashers in a thrilling five-set marquee matchup of the 2026 PVL All-Filipino Conference Siklab Series at the packed Araneta Coliseum.

The jubilation was justified on all fronts, as in the history of this moneymaking, crowd-drawing rivalry, the two-time silver medalist Choco Mucho has only beaten the 11-time champion Creamline twice in 21 meetings dating back to the Flying Titans’ inception in 2019.

Though the historic win certainly meant a lot to every Choco Mucho player who helped forge the late escape, none took the win more emotionally than Jewel Encarnacion, who was later seen in tears as she was interviewed on-court as the Player of the Game.

blocks.caption: Meet Jewel Encarnacion, Choco Mucho’s hidden gem in PVL title pursuit

blocks.text: For stars of the Rebisco-owned teams like Sisi Rondina-Rosales, Eya Laure, Jema Galanza, and Alyssa Valdez, game-based awards like this come as second nature. But for unheralded role players like Encarnacion, each recognition counts for a whole lot more.

“I cried because this is the first time I was named Player of the Game in my PVL career,” the former UP star told reporters in Filipino. “It was made all the sweeter because we got the win, we won against our sister team, and that this is a champion team.”

Though 10 points and 9 excellent receptions are modest numbers in a pro league setting, Encarnacion’s efforts shone especially bright as she helped Choco Mucho most in the closeout fifth set, when Laure was unable to be at her best due to a noticeable back issue.

It was a textbook “next-man-up” call successfully answered, and at a time when PVL roster spots are hard to come by due to multiple team disbandments in recent years, role players like Encarnacion would certainly love to hold onto any recognition that comes their way.

“I’m not trying to think that I have to fill a big role, because that’s just added pressure,” she continued. “I’m just telling myself that I have to just do what I do and perform. I just have to show my strengths and minimize my weaknesses. It’s just filling in for one another. Teamwork.”

Already a journeywoman in just her third year, Encarnacion was one of many unintended casualties of the Cignal Super Spikers going on leave last year, shortly after she signed as a free agent following the expiration of her rookie contract with the Galeries Tower Highrisers.

Though she was soon able to latch on with Choco Mucho, she then had to fight for her spot in Dante Alinsunurin’s loaded spiker rotation that already included established outside hitters like Rondina-Rosales, Laure, captain Des Cheng, fellow UP alumna Isa Molde, and Mean Mendrez.

Also loaded with opposite wingers Kat Tolentino, Caitlin Viray, Dindin Manabat, and Ayesha Juegos, Choco Mucho is just another PVL team burdened and spoiled for choice when it comes to fixing rosters game by game like Creamline, Nxled, and other contenders.

At this point, however, Encarnacion is just content on letting the chips fall where they may, as she focuses on contributing, more than surviving, for a team that still welcomed her with open arms despite barely having room to let her in.

“From the first day, I already embraced Choco Mucho the way they embraced me — from my Rebisco family to my teammates, they all embraced me,” she said. “So I just really try my best to give back to their community.
“Everyone’s heart for one another is in the right place, and I’m overjoyed to be a part of all this.” – Rappler.com
